newsitem.title: INDIA: Mitsubishi in $2 bln India telecom talks.
newsitem.headline: Mitsubishi in $2 bln India telecom talks.

text.p: Japan's Mitsubishi Corp is discussing a $2.0 billion telecommunications joint venture project with India's Tata group and RPG Telecom Ltd, a senior Mitsubishi official said on Monday.
"If we get a good proposal in telecom, we are definitely thinking of a new joint venture," Parvesh Gulati, manager of Mitsubishi Corp's New Delhi liaison office, told Reuters in the Indian capital.
"We are discussing a basic telephone deal with the Tatas and RPG. We are currently negotiating," he said without elaborating. He spoke to Reuters at the 12th Indian Engineering Trade Fair.

The Japanese firm was also in talks with India's Essar Steel Ltd and Tata Iron and Steel Co Ltd (TISCO) to set up a joint venture company that would make construction, steel and port equipment, Gulati said.
"That will involve $10 million minimum, but it could mean up to $50 million -- that depends on the project," he said.
Mitsubishi was discussing building India's first methyl methacrylate (MMA) plant with Indian Petrochemicals Corp Ltd and the Aditya Birla group, Gulati said.
A decision on the project, which would entail investment of $150 million to $250 million, was due by year-end, he said.
Mitsubishi was scheduled later this week to a sign a $10 million joint venture agreement with India's JBM Group to produce metal parts for Hyundai Motor Co Ltd, Gulati said.

Mitsubishi Chemical Corp, a subsidiary of Mitsubishi Corp, was in the process of negotiating a $350 million contract for a turn-key petrochemicals plant in Haldia town, in the eastern state of West Bengal, Gulati said. He gave no other details.
